AGENDA ITEM #8


MEETING DATE: October 7, 2026
TO:                Board of Directors
FROM:              Jillian Steward, Director of Human Resources & Risk Management
SUBJECT:           District's Workforce Vacancies, Recruitment, and Retention Efforts


                                     APPROVED BY:
                                                       Brian C. Wright, General Manager


RECOMMENDATION:
a.) Conduct a Public Hearing regarding the District's Workforce Vacancies,
Recruitment, and Retention Efforts in compliance with AB 2561; and

b.) Provide feedback to staff

BACKGROUND:
To address the widespread and significant problem job vacancies in the public sector
pose to the State of California, Governor Newsom signed Assembly Bill 2561 (AB 2561)
on September 22, 2024. AB 2561 creates new requirements for public agencies to
report before the governing board on vacant positions as well as recruitment and
retention efforts through a public hearing at least once per fiscal year. If the governing
board will be adopting an annual or multiyear budget during the fiscal year, the
presentation shall be made prior to the adoption of the final budget. As part of the
hearing, public agencies, including the District, must identify any challenges and
potential necessary changes to policies, procedures, and recruitment activities to
overcome these challenges. This was last presented to the Board through a Public
Hearing on October 1, 2025.

 If the number of budgeted job vacancies represented by a single bargaining unit meets
or exceeds 20 percent of the total number of authorized full-time positions, the public
agency shall, upon request of the recognized employee organization, include additional
information during the public hearing. This information includes total number of job
vacancies within a bargaining unit, total number of applicants, average number of days
to complete the hiring process, and opportunities to improve compensation and other
working conditions. The recognized employee organization for a bargaining unit shall
be entitled to make a presentation at the public hearing.

 At the September 02, 2026, regularly scheduled Board Meeting, the Board approved
the scheduling of a Public Hearing to be held on October 7, 2026, in accordance with
AB 2561 to present the District’s Workforce Vacancies, Recruitment and Retention
efforts.

RECOMMENDATION:
Reschedule the Electric System Master Plan CEQA Public Hearing from October 7,
2026, to November 4, 2026, at 6:00pm, or as soon thereafter, to receive public
comment on the Proposed Negative Declaration.

BACKGROUND:
The Electric System Master Plan is the District's comprehensive long-range planning
document for the electric utility and establishes the strategic framework for maintaining
safe, reliable, resilient, and financially sustainable electric service.


At the August 5, 2026, Board meeting, District staff and NV5 presented an overview of
the Draft Electric System Master Plan during a Board workshop. The Board received
the presentation and provided feedback prior to initiation of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review and adoption process.

Following the workshop, NV5 completed the CEQA Initial Study for the Electric System
Master Plan. The Initial Study determined that adoption of the Master Plan would not
result in significant environmental impacts and supports a Proposed Negative
Declaration.

At the September 2, 2026, Board meeting, the Board approved the Electric System
Master Plan CEQA Initial Study, authorized circulation of the Proposed Negative
Declaration for public review, and scheduled a Public Hearing for October 7, 2026, at
6:00pm, or as soon thereafter, to receive public comment on the Proposed Negative
Declaration.

FROM:                  Steven Keates, Utility Resource Strategies Manager
                       Brian Wright, General Manager
SUBJECT:               Adopt Resolution 2026-16 approving the submission and attesting to the
                       veracity of the 2025 Power Source Disclosure (PSD) Report and Power
                       Content Label (PCL)


                                             APPROVED BY:
                                                                  Brian C. Wright, General Manager


RECOMMENDATION:
Adopt Resolution 2026-16 approving the submission and attesting to the veracity of the 2025 Power
Source Disclosure (PSD) Report and Power Content Label (PCL).

BACKGROUND:
In 1997, Senate Bill (SB) 1305 established California’s Power Source Disclosure Program (codified
in Public Utilities Code sections 398.1 to 398.5), directing retail electricity suppliers to disclose
energy source mix and environmental impact to consumers. California Energy Commission (CEC)
regulations require retail suppliers to submit annual Power Source Disclosure reports and make the
Power Content Label available to retail customers.

While CEC regulations mandate an annual third-party Certified Public Accountant (CPA) audit to
verify energy purchases, Publicly Owned Utilities (POUs) are exempt if their governing board
formally approves the submission and attests to the veracity of the data. Adopting the proposed
resolution satisfies state mandates while saving the District the expense of an external CPA
audit. The District's Board has historically adopted resolutions to satisfy this State mandate.


ANALYSIS AND BODY:
District staff compiled procurement data for calendar year 2025 from verified supplier records
provided by Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) and Western Area Power
Administration (WAPA). In addition, the board approved retaining Rincon in July 2026 to provide
independent third party verification of the District's electricity transactions for annual reporting to the
California Air Resources Board (CARB) under state Greenhouse Gas (GHG) reporting rules. Staff
has verified the accuracy of these submissions. References to the Power Content Label will be
abbreviated using “PCL”.

                    2026 Physical Security Plan

                                                         Brian C. Wright, General Manager


RECOMMENDATION:
Adopt Resolution No. 2026-17 approving the 2026 Physical Security Plan and authorize
the General Manager or designee to provide the required notice of adoption and
program review documentation to the California Public Utilities Commission Safety and
Enforcement Division.

BACKGROUND:
California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) Decision 19-01-018 establishes physical
security requirements for California electric utilities, including publicly owned utilities
(POUs). The Decision requires utilities to identify electric distribution facilities that may
merit special protection, evaluate physical security risks, develop appropriate mitigation
measures, and obtain an independent third-party review of the resulting Physical
Security Plan (Plan).


The District’s previous Physical Security Plan was completed in 2021. CPUC Decision
19-01-018 requires POUs to conduct a program review of their Security Plan and
associated physical security program every five years following initial approval by their
governing body. Following Board adoption, notice of the Plan adoption must be
provided to the CPUC Safety and Enforcement Division within 30 days.

CPUC Decision 19-01-018 provides that a POU’s notice of final Plan adoption may
consist of a copy of a signed resolution, ordinance, or letter by a responsible elected or
appointed official or utility director. Staff recommends adoption by resolution to provide
a clear and formal record of the Board’s adoption of the Plan for transmittal to the
CPUC.

Consistent with the five-year review cycle, the District has completed its 2026 review
and update of the Physical Security Plan. The updated Plan evaluates seven District
facilities against the CPUC criteria and identifies the Truckee Substation and Martis
Valley Substation as Covered Distribution Facilities. The Primary Control Center is also
included because it will provide supervisory and operational control of the Covered

associated with the general manager's employment agreement, Staff is recommending

BACKGROUND:
The District has a long history of stewardship and collaboration in managing water
resources. A major tenant of local water resource management has been to use the
best available science to inform the decision-making process. This has resulted in
decades of monitoring and scientific study, including the Desert Research Institute’s
Martis Valley groundwater model/report as part of the Federal Truckee River Basin
Study. This effort was supported by the District, Northstar Community Services District -
NCSD, and Placer County Water Agency - PCWA (Local Water Agencies) and was a
key component of the collaboratively adopted 2013 Martis Valley Groundwater
Management Plan (GMP). This effort was temporarily halted when the Martis Valley
Groundwater Basin was initially included in the Sustainable Groundwater Management
Act (SGMA) in 2014 as a Medium Priority Basin, and then removed in 2019 when
reclassified as Very Low Priority.

The three Local Water Agencies worked with our local partners to develop a plan to go
back to the GMP framework in 2019. This included updating the Stakeholder Working
Group list to reflect the local agencies or groups with a direct interest in Martis Valley
groundwater resources. In general, the stakeholders fall into three categories: local
public agencies; major water users/pumpers; and local non-profits/interest groups.

A GMP Stakeholder Working Group kick-off meeting was held in October 2019, where
the three Local Water Agencies reviewed the 2013 Martis Valley GMP and the key
meetings and actions that would occur going forward. This includes an annual report
tracking the performance and long-term sustainability of the groundwater basin, along
with an update to the GMP to occur during 2024. It was agreed that the start of the
GMP would now be in 2019. It was also agreed that the first GMP annual report would
cover the past two water years (October - September 2017/2018 and 2018/2019) which
would provide continuity from the last SGMA annual report. This GMP annual report
